value.hook: When narrowing registration snapshots, checking carried ownership evidence, or changing RelatedSeats
value.title: Related-row queries need a consumer sufficiency proof

sections.name: body
sections.value:
When replacing a whole-roster registration snapshot with list_related, prove two different claims: the SQL returns RelatedSeats::matches exactly, and that relation contains every row each consumer can inspect. The shared fake/SQLite contract proves only the first.

For #227 f91b3ffffea45b678dd35a8d9460d4a9e50703a0, the registration consumer trace is in its reviewer output. Current checks consult explicit/carried IDs, matching harness_session, pane or PID. In particular, observed dead owners and spawn prebinds must be carried by ID: otherwise concurrent changes to their other keys could hide owner drift. PID must include other process start times for paneless conflict checks. Preserve retired rows and ID order. Existing continuity is checked on the selected row's session/spawn/process fields; it does not recursively follow retired IDs or parent chains through the roster.

ID minting is the exception to the related-row rule: check every memorable candidate through the global primary key under the registration lock, including retired rows. The narrow snapshot cannot establish global absence. Future predicates outside these relations must widen the relation or perform their own read.

F182/#225 and F185/#227 correctness review passed with live after-deploy measurements owed to performance, not with an independent reviewer CPU measurement. F184/#226 passed the exact eight-leaf callerless read path. All verdicts use the canonical output writer and full head; their outputs contain the CI artifact IDs and observed test execution.

Magic wand: a small regression comparing registration outcomes using a full-roster adapter and a related-row adapter would defend consumer sufficiency, which SQL-versus-matches tests alone cannot. This is an optional future harness improvement, not a C34 merge gate or an implemented fixture.
